schema: predictions for the two-region conduction benchmark, generated by checks/make_predictions.py
solver: chtMultiRegionFoam, two solid regions (no fluid region): right = isotropic (listed first, solved first), left = anisotropic constAnIso

notation.c: stencil conductance = Gamma_nn * Cp * deltaCoeffs (what the Laplacian uses)
notation.b: coupling conductance = kappa_BC * deltaCoeffs (what the coupled condition hands over)
notation.rho_XY: (c_X/b_X)/(c_Y/b_Y) = heat received by X over heat released by Y

predictions.title: Weights of the two-sided mixed condition
predictions.claim: The value fraction written by each side is KDeltaNbr/(KDeltaNbr + KDelta) with KDelta = kappa_BC * deltaCoeffs; for the scalar option on the constAnIso solid kappa_BC is the Frobenius norm of the principal conductivities.
predictions.measure: valueFraction entry of the written T boundary field of the anisotropic region
predictions.refuted_if: the written valueFraction corresponds to 0.8 or 28 instead of 28.0228

predictions.title: Patch temperature is the pre-solve mixed value
predictions.claim: After a region is solved the temperature stored on its coupled patch is f*T_nbr_cell + (1-f)*T_own_cell with the own-cell value from BEFORE that solve; it is not recomputed from enthalpy, and the enthalpy patch value is overwritten by H(T_patch).

inputs.case: slab with Cp(T) in the isotropic region, one time step of 0.0025 s, 5 + 5 cells, T = 300 / 350 K

predictions.measure: value entry of the coupled patch in the written T field after one step
predictions.refuted_if: the written value equals THE(f h(T_nbr) + (1-f) h_cell) (about 331.39 K) instead of 330.769 K

onestep.note: the written value equals the pre-solve mixed value; it is neither the post-solve mixed value nor the temperature recovered from the mixed enthalpy (about 331.39 K)

evidence.note: the emulator reproduces the Cp(T) cases to 1e-9 K only with this rule

predictions.title: Flux mismatch factor of the scalar option against orientation
predictions.claim: With kappaMethod solidThermo the neighbour receives ||K||_F/(n.K.n) times the heat the anisotropic region releases (same-instant fluxes; the energy books agree after the staggering term of P08 is removed).

inputs.geometry: two slabs in series, x in [-2 mm, 0] anisotropic, [0, 2 mm] isotropic, one-dimensional

anisotropic.rotation: principal axis 1 at angle theta from the interface normal, about z

inputs.outer_boundaries: zeroGradient (adiabatic; exact here because the field is one-dimensional)

predictions.measure: storage change of each region (closed adiabatic pair): dU_iso/(-dU_aniso), plus dt*C_X*(T_Y1^N - T_Y1^0) (P08)
predictions.refuted_if: the de-staggered ratio differs from the formula by more than solver tolerance at any angle

predictions.title: Isotropic conductivity entered as a three-component vector
predictions.claim: For kappa (k k k) through constAnIso the scalar option uses sqrt(3) k, so the mismatch factor is sqrt(3) on every face, not 1; the directional option gives 1.
predictions.measure: as P03
predictions.refuted_if: the scalar option gives 1 for (k k k)

predictions.title: The mismatch factor does not depend on mesh, time step or the neighbour
predictions.claim: The same-instant flux ratio is exactly (c_X/b_X)/(c_Y/b_Y): no dependence on cell size, time step, the neighbour's conductivity or an interface layer resistance.  Only the staggering term (P08) changes with dt and mesh.
predictions.measure: as P03 for each variant
predictions.refuted_if: the de-staggered ratio drifts with any of the three parameters
predictions.status: confirmed_by_openfoam_run (mesh, dt, neighbour conductivity); emulator_only (layer resistance)

predictions.title: Directional option is conservative on a slab at every angle
predictions.claim: With kappaMethod directionalSolidThermo the ratio is 1 for any orientation of K when the temperature is uniform along the interface (the tangential term of P11 vanishes).
predictions.measure: as P03
predictions.refuted_if: ratio differs from 1 after removing the staggering term

predictions.title: Steady two-layer slab: the scalar option converges to a different transmission problem
predictions.claim: With fixed end temperatures the scalar option gives the wall temperature of a slab whose solid conductivity is ||K||_F, on any mesh and for any orientation; the fluid-side flux is k_f (T_w - T_R)/L_f and the solid-side flux is smaller by (n.K.n)/||K||_F.

expected.formula: T_w = (k_c T_L/L_s + k_f T_R/L_f)/(k_c/L_s + k_f/L_f), k_c = ||K||_F (scalar) or n.K.n (directional)

predictions.measure: coupled-patch temperature and the end-cell conduction fluxes at steady state
predictions.refuted_if: T_w depends on the mesh, or on theta for the scalar option

predictions.title: Staggering term of one coupling pass (telescoping identity)
predictions.claim: With one pass per step, region X solved first: E_X = -rho_XY E_Y - dt C_X (T_Y1^N - T_Y1^0) exactly (constant properties, constant dt, Euler), where T_Y1 is the first-cell temperature of the region solved second and C_X = c_X b_Y/(b_X + b_Y).
predictions.measure: region storage changes and the first-cell temperature of the second region at start and end
predictions.refuted_if: the identity fails beyond solver tolerance, or the term does not scale with dt

predictions.title: Closed adiabatic pair: equilibrium temperature
predictions.claim: T_eq = (M_X T_X0 + (rho_XY M_Y + dt C_X) T_Y0)/(M_X + rho_XY M_Y + dt C_X), M = rho Cp L per unit area.
predictions.measure: uniform temperature at the end of the run
predictions.refuted_if: the scalar-option equilibrium is the energy-conserving value

predictions.title: Coupling passes remove the staggering term but not the conservation defect
predictions.claim: Each extra pass (nOuterCorrectors) multiplies the staggering drift by a contraction factor rho_c < 1 (lumped upper estimate D_X D_Y/((1+D_X)(1+D_Y)), D = C dt/(rho Cp dx)); reversing the solve order flips its sign. The factor rho_XY of P03 is unchanged by either.
predictions.measure: dU_iso/(-dU_aniso) without any correction
predictions.refuted_if: the raw ratio does not approach 1 with passes, or the scalar-option factor changes with passes

predictions.title: Oblique patch test: the stock directional option fails
predictions.claim: When n is not a principal direction and the temperature varies along the interface, the directional option exchanges only the normal part: the two normal fluxes balance to round-off, the solid additionally carries the explicit tangential flux, and the interface creates energy at the rate integral of (K n)_t . grad_t T, which for a planar interface with constant K equals K_xy times the temperature difference between the two ends of the interface (first solid cell layer). The exact piecewise-linear solution is not reproduced.

inputs.geometry: two 10 mm x 10 mm squares sharing the plane x = 0; anisotropic region at x < 0
inputs.cells: 16 x 16 per region (also 8 x 8 and 32 x 32)

anisotropic.rotation: axis 1 at angle theta from +x, about z

inputs.exact_solution: T = T0 + A x + B y (x<0), T0 + A_f x + B y (x>0), k_f A_f = K_xx A + K_xy B
inputs.outer_boundaries: fixed value from the exact solution on every outer boundary
inputs.steady_state: pseudo-time: rho = 1, Cp = 1000 in both regions, dt = 0.05 s, 3000 steps

expected.imbalance_formula: K_xy * B * H  [W per metre depth]

predictions.tolerance: imbalance and normal-part balance: 1e-8 W/m; temperature errors: 1e-9 K against the emulator values
predictions.measure: isotropic side: stock wallHeatFlux; anisotropic side: K_xx*snGrad(T) + K_xy*(dT/dy)_cell summed over the patch (the solver's own operator, Section F); temperatures against the exact linear field
predictions.refuted_if: the directional option reproduces the linear solution to round-off at theta not in {0, 90}

predictions.title: The oblique error does not converge under mesh refinement
predictions.claim: The error of P11 is a consistency error of the interface condition: it stays O(1) as the mesh is refined (the discrete solution converges to the problem with k_f dT_f/dn = (n.K.n) dT_s/dn instead of the co-normal flux).
predictions.measure: as P11
predictions.refuted_if: the maximum temperature error falls at first or second order with refinement
predictions.status: confirmed_by_openfoam_run (8, 16, 32 cells; note the emulator table uses A = B = 1000 K/m)

predictions.title: Co-normal correction passes the patch test to round-off
predictions.claim: Adding q_tan = -(n.Gamma - (n.Gamma.n) n).grad(h) of the anisotropic side to the interface balance of BOTH sides (stock qr / qrNbr entries fed by the function object coNormalInterfaceFlux) makes the coupling consistent and conservative: the linear solution is reproduced on every mesh and at every angle.
predictions.measure: as P11
predictions.refuted_if: a residual error remains that does not fall with the linear-solver tolerance

predictions.title: Sheared one-dimensional configuration: closed-form wall-temperature error
predictions.claim: For T = phi(x) + B y (uniform tangential gradient, interface much taller than the slab thicknesses) the stock directional option gives a wall temperature that is too high by K_xy B/(K_xx/L_s + k_f/L_f), independent of the mesh.
predictions.tolerance: approached as H/L grows (emulator: 3.25, 7.82, 8.83 K for H/L = 1, 4, 16)
predictions.measure: patch temperature at mid-height minus the exact value, for increasing interface height; or a cyclic pair with a fixedJump of B*H on T (not tried)
predictions.refuted_if: the mid-height error does not approach the closed form as the interface is made taller

predictions.title: Coincidence to avoid when designing the oblique test
predictions.claim: At theta = 45 deg with equal normal and tangential gradients (A = B) the scalar option is almost exact, because K_xx + K_xy = k1 there and ||K||_F is within 0.08 % of k1.  A benchmark must not use A = B at 45 deg.

inputs.case: patch (emulator), A = B = 1000 K/m, theta = 45 deg, scalar option

predictions.title: Closed curved interface with Cartesian orthotropy
predictions.claim: For a circular cylinder of a material with K = diag(k_x, k_y) in fixed Cartesian axes, the stock directional option creates energy at the rate (k_x - k_y) * pi * a_2 per unit length, a_2 being the cos(2 phi) Fourier coefficient of the first-solid-cell temperature around the circumference.  It is zero only if the wall temperature has no second harmonic.

inputs.geometry: cylinder in a coupled surrounding region; K constant in Cartesian axes

expected.formula: oint (K n)_t . grad_t T ds = (k_x - k_y) pi a_2

predictions.tolerance: to discretisation error of the circle
predictions.measure: two-sided balance of Section F on a polar or O-grid mesh
predictions.refuted_if: the measured imbalance does not follow the second harmonic of the wall temperature
predictions.status: derived_only (the integral identity is symbolic, check S7; no run on a curved interface)

symbolic.statement: oint (K n)_t . grad_t T ds = (k_x - k_y) pi a_2 for K = diag(k_x,k_y) on a circle (harmonics up to 3)

predictions.title: zeroGradient is not adiabatic on an oblique anisotropic solid
predictions.claim: The explicit off-normal flux is added on every non-coupled boundary face, so a zeroGradient (or symmetry-like) wall whose normal is not a principal direction carries the heat flux (K n)_t . grad_t T.  A closed-box conservation test must use aligned K or account for it.

inputs.case: closed two-dimensional box, theta = 45 deg, zeroGradient everywhere

expected.note: no NET leak while the field stays uniform along the wall direction (through-flux in at one wall, out at the other); net leak K_xy * [(T_E - T_W)_north row - (T_E - T_W)_south row] otherwise

predictions.measure: total energy drift of a closed box with an initial field that varies in y, compared with the aligned case
predictions.refuted_if: total energy is conserved (beyond the staggering term) for a y-dependent field at theta = 45 deg
predictions.status: derived_only (code path confirmed by P13; the one box run made here had a y-uniform field and showed only the staggering drift, as the formula predicts, so it does not discriminate)

predictions.title: Temperature-dependent Cp: second, first-order interface imbalance
predictions.claim: With consistent conductances the region whose Cp depends on T receives the conservative flux times meanCp[T_own,T_nbr]/Cp(T_wall); for linear Cp the relative defect is c1 (1/2 - f)(T_nbr - T_own)/Cp(T_wall). It is proportional to the first-cell temperature difference, hence first order in mesh spacing, and vanishes for f = 1/2.
predictions.measure: dU_iso/(-dU_aniso) with dU_iso from rho*(h - h0)
predictions.refuted_if: the ratio is 1 with Cp(T), or its deviation from 1 does not halve when the spacing halves
predictions.status: confirmed_by_openfoam_run (OpenFOAM equals the emulator to 1e-9 K; the per-step formula is checked in the emulator)

predictions.title: Size of the Cp(T) defect in the demonstration case
predictions.claim: On the medium mesh the fluid receives about 0.37 % less than the solid releases over the 260 s discharge (2.8 J per quarter model), about half from the can wall and half from the end caps; at 260 s the instantaneous defect is 0.45 % (medium) and 0.30 % (fine).

inputs.source: archived fields of a one-corrector run with the velocity limiter, medium mesh (fluid T patch entries and wallHeatFlux)

predictions.tolerance: order of magnitude: trapezoid rule over 10 s snapshots, and the archived fluid solution is not reliable
predictions.measure: re-run with a constant-Cp fluid (defect must vanish) or evaluate the two-sided balance of Section F per time step
predictions.refuted_if: a constant-Cp run leaves a solid-side residual of the same size

predictions.title: Size of the staggering term in the demonstration case
predictions.claim: About 0.13 J per quarter model (0.5 J for the whole cell) at the mean time step of 5.4 ms: negligible against the Cp(T) defect and four orders of magnitude below the scalar-option defect.
predictions.tolerance: order of magnitude (constant conductance and mean dt assumed)
predictions.measure: energyCoupling iterations or nOuterCorrectors 2 in the top-level fvSolution: the term must fall by the contraction factor

predictions.title: Stock wallHeatFlux on the anisotropic side reports ||K||_F/(n.K.n) times the true normal flux
predictions.claim: The function object multiplies snGrad(h) by the scalar thermo alpha = ||K||_F/Cp.  With the scalar coupling its value equals minus the neighbour-side value (the books appear closed while the solid's true release is smaller by the factor); with the directional coupling it over-reports the solid flux by the factor and omits the tangential part.
predictions.measure: postProcessing/<region>/wallHeatFlux integral on the coupled patch against the region storage change
predictions.refuted_if: the solid-side function object equals the storage-based flux with the directional option

predictions.title: Fluid-side (isotropic-side) function object is an exact book for that region
predictions.claim: Summing dt * integral(wallHeatFlux) over the time steps on the isotropic side reproduces that region's storage change to solver tolerance (constant properties).
predictions.measure: as stated

predictions.title: Isotropy guard
predictions.claim: solidThermo::isotropic() is false for constAnIso and tabulatedAnIso; a check of kappaMethod solidThermo against it stops the run before the first step.

inputs.case: patch, theta = 45 deg, kappaMethod solidThermo, function object coNormalInterfaceFlux with errors strict

expected.result: FOAM FATAL ERROR before the first time step; a warning only if the function object is not strict

predictions.measure: solver log

evidence.result: FOAM FATAL ERROR raised by coNormalInterfaceFlux::checkGuard before the first time step (function object entry errors strict); without errors strict the same message is a warning and the run continues

predictions.title: Demonstration re-run with the scalar option: per-patch energy ratio
predictions.claim: If the scalar-option run is repeated with the interface split into side and end patches, the fluid-to-solid energy ratio is 35.03 on the side and 1.0008 on the ends (times the Cp factor of P18, about 0.997 and 0.98), so overall E_fluid/E_solid = 1.0008 + 34.03 * (fraction of the solid's interface energy leaving through the side).
predictions.measure: storage-based solid audit per patch is not possible; use the Section F flux on each solid patch against the fluid-side function object on the matching fluid patch
predictions.refuted_if: the side-patch ratio differs from 35.0 by more than the Cp factor
predictions.status: derived_only (the slab runs confirm the factor; the 18650 case was not run)

predictions.title: Solid non-orthogonal correctors are not applied in chtMultiRegionFoam v2606
predictions.claim: solid/solveSolid.H assembles and solves the solid enthalpy equation once per pass; nNonOrthogonalCorrectors of the solid region is read but unused, so the explicit off-normal tensor flux and the mesh non-orthogonal correction lag by one pass.

inputs.case: any; demonstration has nNonOrthogonalCorrectors 1 in system/battery/fvSolution

predictions.measure: count "Solving for h" lines after "Solving for solid region" in one time step of the log
predictions.refuted_if: two h solves per step appear for the solid
predictions.status: confirmed (source reading and the archived production log, which shows one DICPCG h solve per step for the battery)

evidence.log: solver log of the same run (not in this repository)

predictions.title: Implicit (assembled) coupling path
predictions.claim: useImplicit selects the diffusivity through the same kappaMethod switch (temperatureCoupledBase::alpha), so the scalar option is expected to be defective there too; the size and form of the defect were not derived.

inputs.case: slab with useImplicit true on both sides

predictions.measure: repeat P03, P06 and P11 with useImplicit true
